criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: `ProducerOutput` gains `criteria_check: Vec<CriterionCheckOutput>`, and each entry has `criterion`, `status` (Met or Unmet) and `evidence`. The existing schema test now asserts that `producer_schema()["properties"]["criteria_check"]` is present and that the field is in `required`.

criteria.criterion: crates/athena-context/prompts/producer.md tells the producer to check its work against each accepted acceptance criterion and to report the result in criteria_check, and says that an unmet criterion is sent back once and then fails the job.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: the prompt has a new bullet, "Check your work against each acceptance criterion and report it in `criteria_check` ... An unmet or missing one is sent back once, then fails the job."

criteria.criterion: produce_and_verify in crates/athena-core/src/run.rs sends a report back to the producer when any accepted criterion is unmet or missing from criteria_check. The send-back brief names every such criterion, and the producer's UI line says so.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: `unmet_criteria()` returns each accepted criterion that has no entry with exact (trimmed) matching text and status Met. Any such criterion triggers a send-back. The brief lists each one as `- {criterion}` under "Criteria not met or not reported". The UI line `producer   sent back: ...` includes "acceptance criteria not met or not reported: \"...\"", and the new test asserts that line contains the criterion text.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked`. A new lifecycle test has the scripted producer first report one criterion unmet and then report all criteria met. It asserts that the producer runs twice before the first Verifier invocation, that the send-back brief text contains the unmet criterion, that the job lands, and that the verifier is never the first to see the unmet criterion.
criteria.evidence: The test `a_criterion_unmet_before_verification_goes_back_to_the_producer_not_the_verifier` passed in both runs. It asserts the job Landed, that there are exactly 2 Producer roles before the first Verifier, that the second brief contains `## Sent back` and `- <unmet criterion>` but not the met one, and that the UI line names the criterion. It also checks that the verifier's input contains no send-back or `criteria_check` text.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked`. A second new test has the producer still report a criterion unmet after the send-back. It asserts that the job ends Failed with a reason naming the criterion and that no Verifier invocation happened.
criteria.evidence: The test `a_criterion_still_unmet_after_the_send_back_fails_the_job_unverified` passed. It asserts the job is Failed, the reason contains texts[1], there were 2 producer runs, and the roles contain no Verifier. A third test, `a_criterion_missing_from_the_report_counts_as_unmet`, also passed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`. All three pass, and the existing lifecycle tests still pass after the fake agent and test helpers were updated to emit criteria_check.
criteria.evidence: All three commands, run in this snapshot, passed: every test binary reported ok with 0 failed (the lifecycle binary had 38 passed), clippy finished clean, and fmt printed nothing. `fake.rs`, `common/mod.rs` and `run_pin_tests.rs` now emit `criteria_check`.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the pre-verification criteria check.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: under Added, there is a new entry beginning "A criteria check before verification". It describes the new field, the shared send-back, failing the job before the verifier runs, pinned studies, and that older records still read.

findings.summary: The producer prompt was reworded beyond the new rule, and the rewording dropped some guidance.
findings.evidence: Besides adding the criteria_check bullet, the diff shortens six existing lines. It drops the list of which non-Rust files policy tests read (boundary words, unlisted file kinds, defaults.toml, study model.json), drops "say what is missing" from the requirements-map rule, and changes "the owner's private files" to "private files". The request did not ask for any of this.

findings.summary: The test's check that the verifier was not first to see the unmet criterion is only indirect.
findings.evidence: The final assertion only checks that the verifier's input lacks `## Sent back` and `criteria_check`. That holds anyway, because the verifier is never shown the producer's report. The assertion that matters is that both producer runs come before the first Verifier, and the test has it.

summary: The change does what was asked. The producer's report now has a required `criteria_check` list. In `produce_and_verify`, any accepted criterion that is marked unmet or missing from that list goes back to the producer. This uses the existing send-back budget, and every such criterion is named in one brief. A criterion still unmet after that fails the job before the verifier runs. Three new lifecycle tests cover: an unmet criterion that is sent back and fixed before the verifier's first run, one still unmet after the send-back (the job fails and the verifier never runs), and one missing from the list. I ran `cargo test --locked` in this snapshot and all tests passed, including the new ones. `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` were both clean. Every changed file is on the deliverables list. My one finding is minor: the producer prompt was also reworded in places the request didn't ask for, and that rewording dropped some guidance.
